problem:
I changed my university password this morning.
Now my Windows laptop won't connect to campus Wi-Fi,
but my phone still works.

solution.diagnosis: The Windows laptop failed to connect to campus Wi-Fi because it is still using cached old credentials. The phone worked because it does not cache Wi-Fi passwords in the same way.
steps: Forget the 'eduroam' network in Windows Wi-Fi settings: Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > Select 'eduroam' > Click 'Forget'.
Reconnect to 'eduroam' using the new password: Click 'Connect' after forgetting the network, then enter the updated university password.
Verify the university account is active: Check with your institution's IT support or account management system to ensure the password change was successful and the account is not locked.
solution.additional_notes: Windows may prompt for the password again after reconnecting. If issues persist, contact your university's IT helpdesk for further assistance. Phones typically do not cache Wi-Fi credentials, which is why they work without intervention.
